entities.summary:
Philip, the Antipope, played a pivotal role in the tumultuous landscape of the late 8th century. As the leader of the opposition to Pope Stephen III, Philip's brief tenure on the papacy had a lasting impact on the politics of the Western Roman Empire.


The events of Philip's papacy were marked by a series of power struggles with his supporters and detractors, ultimately leading to his ouster on July 31, 768. This event set the stage for the rise of Charlemagne, who would go on to shape the destiny of Western Christendom.


Despite his brief time in office, Philip's legacy extended beyond the confines of the papal throne. His actions influenced the politics of the Carolingian Empire, which would become a dominant force in European history for centuries to come.


In the annals of history, Philip's name serves as a reminder of the complex web of power dynamics that characterized the medieval period. His story is a testament to the enduring power of human ambition and the fragility of even the most powerful institutions.
